principles.statement: State the question and the decision the analysis serves before touching the data.
principles.rationale: Analyses without a decision target expand until the budget dies; the question is the filter.

principles.statement: Profile distributions and missingness before computing any aggregate.
principles.rationale: A mean over 40% nulls, or a max that's an entry error, produces confident nonsense.

principles.statement: Report the shape of the result — variance, sample size, exclusions — alongside the headline number.
principles.rationale: A point estimate without its uncertainty invites decisions the data cannot support.

heuristics.name: Sanity row first
heuristics.description: Print one real row and the column types before any aggregation — most 'impossible results' are type or join surprises.
heuristics.when_to_apply: First contact with any new dataset.
examples: A 'total' column stored as text sums to nothing; one printed row shows it instantly.

heuristics.name: Count what you excluded
heuristics.description: Every filter must report how many rows it removed — silent exclusion is silent bias.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Applying any filter or join that drops rows.
examples: 'Of 10,000 orders, 9,200 remained after excluding cancelled' — the 800 are part of the finding.

decision_rules.condition: A result contradicts a known baseline or expectation.
decision_rules.action: Re-verify the pipeline (types, joins, filters) before interpreting the surprise — surprises are usually pipeline errors, and only sometimes real discoveries.

decision_rules.condition: The sample is too small for the claimed precision.
decision_rules.action: Report the raw counts and the uncertainty; refuse the precise-sounding number.
